EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
  MINUTES
  September 26, 2016

CALL TO ORDER
CHAIRWOMAN SCHMITZ called the meeting to order, the time being 7:00 p.m. in the Rolling
Hills Estates City Council Chambers.

COMMITTEE MEMBERS PRESENT
Chairman Velveth Schmitz
Vicki Shinn
Carrie Silvano
Susan Brtis
Bill Kemp
Patricia Harik

COMMITTEE MEMBERS ABSENT – EXCUSED
Pam Schachter
Carol Dean-Porter
Victor Yoo
Lisa Hawkins

STAFF MEMBERS PRESENT
Andy Clark, Community Services Director

DRAFT MINUTES OF JULY 19, 2016
MEMBER SHINN requested a correction on Page 3, for the first sentence in Paragraph 3:

“MEMBER SHINN stated that a Dressage Arena should be considered for construction in
Chandler Park.”

MEMBER SHINN moved, seconded by MEMBER SILVANO

  TO APPROVE THE DRAFT MINUTES OF THE JULY 19, 2016 EQUESTRIAN
  COMMITTEE MEETING AS AMENDED.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRWOMAN SCHMITZ SO ORDERED.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
SEPTEMBER 26, 2016  1
 AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA
None.

PROPOSED NEW DRESSAGE ARENA ON PALOS VERDES LANDFILL

The Community Services Director reviewed the staff report and thanked Field Representative,
Rebekah Kim from Supervisor Knabe’s office and Ethan Laden, On-Site Engineer from the
Sanitation Districts of Los Angeles County for being in attendance. Various mitigation
measures were outlined should the proposed riding arena be constructed as follows: 1) use of
landscaping to create a natural screening; 2) installation of an arena sprinkling system with
manual and automatic controls; 3) use of low dust, GGT arena footing material; 4) installation
of a perimeter fence enclosure around the arena fence; 5) prohibiting light fixtures; and 6)
installing arena regulation signage with additional rules prohibiting music or sound projection
systems, watering requirements, and prohibiting the turning loose of horses.

In response to CHAIRWOMAN SCHMITZ inquiry, the Community Services Director described
the proposed arena as: 1) maintained operated by the City; 2) maintained and operated by
the Peter Weber Equestrian Center; and 3) hybrids of both maintenance and operational
methods. Three Equestrian Committee Members felt that the proposed arena should be
maintained and operated by the City as a public arena, while two Equestrian Committee
Members believed it should be a hybrid operational method.

MEMBER SHINN stated that the proposed location to construct the arena would experience
safety issues due to the volume of large truck and vehicle traffic which would pass nearby.
Ethan Laden, On-Site Engineer responded that he would be willing to explore other potential
locations on the former landfill to construct a riding arena. Roanwood Homeowners (HOA)
resident, Steve Shinn, stated that the proposed arena would not be a public arena, feels that
there is little interest in dressage riding as indicated by the low use of the Ernie Howlett Park
dressage arena, and opposes an arena being constructed at the proposed site near his home.

Several Roanwood HOA residents including, Betty Woodburn, Ann Bozarth, Mr. & Mrs.
Emberman, and Steve Watts stated that they opposed the construction of the arena in the
proposed location near their homes. HOA resident, Mark Sur felt that the City provided poor
and short notice regarding the proposed riding arena. CHAIRWOMAN SCHMITZ responded
that the City makes a variety of attempts to notify residents of public meetings, minutes from
past meetings, and items on meeting agendas. She encouraged the audience to sign up for
the City’s e-Notification system and select the information which they would like to regularly
receive by email. The CHAIRWOMAN also assured residents that if the proposed riding
arena would be voted by the Equestrian Committee tonight for further consideration that it
would next be reviewed by the Park and Activities Commission, with HOA residents being
notified of this public meeting. And, finally, should the Commission recommend further
consideration by City Council, that the HOA’s residents again would be notified of this public
meeting.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
SEPTEMBER 26, 2016  2
 Field Representative Kim stated that she was pleased that City and residents could come
together to have a full discussion about the proposed riding arena. CHAIRWOMAN
SCHMITZ thanked her and Mr. Laden for attending this meeting.

MEMBER SHINN moved, seconded by MEMBER HARIK

  TO DECLINE THE CONSTRUCTION OF A RIDING ARENA ON THE PROPOSED
  SITE AND TO FORM A SUBCOMMITTEE TO DETERMINE WHETHER THERE ARE
  OTHER MORE SUITABLE LOCATIONS ON THE FORMER PALOS VERDES
  LANDFILL TO CONSTRUCT A RIDING ARENA.

Hearing no objections, CHAIRWOMAN SCHMITZ so ordered.

CITY CELEBRATION EVALUATION
The Community Services Director noted that absent MEMBER SCHACHTER had provided
her written comments, which were shared with the Equestrian Committee at the meeting.
CHAIRWOMAN SCHMITZ thanked MEMBERS SCHACHTER, SHINN, and SILVANO for how
smoothly the equestrian events and activities ran this year. She also thanked the Park and
Activities Commission and the Community Services Director for their planning efforts resulting
in a successful event. The CHAIRWOMAN also asked that during the planning meetings next
year, that a purpose or mission statement for each City Celebration activity be defined with
the goals outlined to achieve that mission. In addition, she believes that the event could have
ended as early as 2:00 p.m., as she noted a significant decline in attendance occurring at that
time.

MEMBER SHINN noted that rakes and water buckets will be needed, in addition to “reserved”
signs in the barn area next year. Also, she believes that one of the interior stalls could be
closed off as a dressing room for equestrians and stage performers to change clothing.
MEMBER KEMP suggested that more venue maps be made available and that they could be
provided on the shuttle busses. MEMBER HARIK reported that arena sprinkling station #4
was not working and suggested that a water truck be rented next year, due to the high winds
that occur each afternoon at Howlett Park, impeding good watering coverage of the arenas.

CHAIRWOMAN SCHMITZ stated that she missed the traditional City Celebration “birthday”
cake and recommended that it be re-considered next year. MEMBER SHINN suggested that
a golf cart circulate among the event patrons selling beverages, as is done at the Portuguese
Bend National Horse Show. In addition, she believes that more portable radios would have
helped better coordinate the equestrian events. MEMBER HARIK suggested that a “stick
horse” event be added next year to the equestrian activities. MEMBER KEMP encouraged
that an opportunity for early registration of the horsemanship and trails class events be set up
to decrease the long lines that occur prior to these events. Finally, CHAIRWOMAN SCHMITZ
recommended that regular announcements from the stage regarding the upcoming equestrian
and stage activities be made next year and that informational signage be increased
throughout the venue.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
SEPTEMBER 26, 2016  3
 EQUESTRIAN FEES SUBCOMMITTEE UPDATE
The Community Services Director reviewed the staff report and thanked the Equestrian Fees
Subcommittee for their work, which included MEMBERS SCHACHTER, KEMP, SILVANO,
and SHINN. A description of three new categories of horse trainers’ fees was reviewed as
follows: Category 1 – Horse trainers in residence at a private facility and do not use the City’s
public arenas ($300); Category 2 – Horse trainers whose primary business is conducted
outside the Palos Verdes Peninsula area, or in a private facility, and uses the City’s public
arenas no more than once per week ($450); and 3) Horse trainers whose business
significantly relies on the City’s public arenas and uses them on a semi-weekly to daily basis
($700 in 2017 and $1,000 in 2018). In addition, the Subcommittee developed Ernie Howlett
Park equestrian center rental fees for individuals or organizations which provided shows for
profit, with fee increases of $100 to $200 depending on the number of facilities rented.

Audience member, Gil Houle, noted that horse shoers are not being charge a Business
License fee in our City. Horse haulers, according to audience member, Larry Lean, are also
not being charged a Business License fee.

MEMBER SHINN moved, seconded by MEMBER HARIK

  1) TO RECOMMEND THAT THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MAKE A
  RECOMMENDATION TO CITY COUNCIL TO APPROVE THE FEES AS STATED IN
  THE STAFF REPORT; AND 2) TO DIRECT THE CITY ATTORNEY TO TAKE THE
  STEPS REQUIRED TO AMEND ORDINANCE SECTION 5.08.100 TO READ THAT
  “PERMIT FEES” SHALL BE SET BY CITY COUNCIL RESOLUTION.

AYES – Schmitz, Shinn, Harik, Kemp, Silvano, and Brtis

NOES – None

ABSTAIN – None

CHAIRWOMAN SCHMITZ reported that the motion carried.

CHANDLER ARENA DRY ERASE BOARD
In response to the Community Services Director’s inquiry, the Equestrian Committee was
unanimous in instituting a rule that horse trainers should not sign up on the Chandler Park
arena’s new dry erase board more than 15 minutes in advance of their lesson(s) period.

EQUESTRIAN ISSUES LOG
HEARING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRWOMAN SCHMITZ RECEIVED AND FILED THE
EQUESTRIAN ISSUES LOG.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
SEPTEMBER 26, 2016  4
 COMMITTEE REPORTS
A.  ADOPT-A-TRAIL REPORTS
None.

B.  COYOTE SIGHTINGS
MEMBER SHINN reported increased sightings of coyotes on the City’s trails. CHAIRWOMAN
SCHMITZ strongly encouraged Committee Members to report coyote sightings to the Los
Angeles County Agricultural Commissioner/Weights & Measures at (626) 575-5471.

FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS
A.  POTENTIAL NEW DRESSAGE ARENA ON PV LANDFIL (Fall 2016 – Per Supervisor
  Knabe’s approval)

B.  NEW PETER WEBER EQUESTRIAN CENTER RESTROOM BUILDING (Fall 2016 –
  After PWEC Grant Reimbursements Received)

C.  POTENTIAL PWEC HORSE TRAILER PARKING AT RECYCLE CENTER (Fall 2016
  - Per Supervisor Knabe’s approval)

ADJOURNMENT
MEMBER SHINN moved, seconded by MEMBER SILVANO

  TO ADJOURN THE EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING.

HEARING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRWOMAN SCHMITZ ADJOURNED THE MEETING.

The meeting adjourned at 8:45 p.m.

Respectfully submitted,

Andy Clark
Community Services Director
